propositions: When two bundles exist for the same S3 ref, git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects the push before writing anything and fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, causing the store to become unclonable and push retries to hang indefinitely.

Upstream's interactive Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles blocks on input() prompts (crashes on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head by side-branching it to an orphan ref, losing events unique to that head — unacceptable for an append-only event log like rebar's ticket store.

A non-interactive auto-doctor must detect the multi-bundle signature, acquire the helper's per-ref S3 lock, enumerate bundles under the lock (TOCTOU guard), fetch all divergent heads locally, fold them losslessly via iterated 2-parent merges (reusing sync's existing reconcile semantics and merge=ours for .bridge_state/*), write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any originals, and never discard a head — ensuring at least one bundle carries full merged history at every crash point.

The doctor runs under rebar's write_lock (serializing against local committers) while holding the helper's S3 per-ref lock (outer, serializing cross-clone repairs), with fixed cycle-free lock ordering; on a real git merge conflict it aborts without deleting remote bundles and surfaces fsck-recover rather than silently dropping a parent.

The optional s3_doctor.py module imports git_remote_s3 and boto3 lazily behind require_s3_helper(), adding no hard S3 dependency to core rebar; all S3 ops (lock, enumerate, delete) route through the helper's own S3Remote and .s3 client, which are already available transitive under the [s3] extra.

Concurrent doctors serialized by the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock: exactly one acquires it, performs the merge-to-single-bundle consolidation, releases it, and all others back off observing lock contention — converging on the winner's collapsed remote on their subsequent push retry, achieving fleet-wide self-healing without a daemon.
